Since \(2=|2^0-3^1|\), it is representable.

All primes below \(41\) are representable:
\[
\begin{aligned}
2&=|2^0-3^1|,\quad 3=|2^2-3^0|,\quad 5=|2^3-3^1|,\\
7&=|2^4-3^2|,\quad 11=|2^4-3^3|,\quad 13=|2^4-3^1|,\\
17&=|2^6-3^4|,\quad 19=|2^3-3^3|,\quad 23=|2^2-3^3|,\\
29&=|2^5-3^1|,\quad 31=|2^5-3^0|,\quad 37=|2^6-3^3|.
\end{aligned}
\]

Now show \(41\) is not representable. Suppose \(|2^a-3^b|=41\).

If \(2^a-3^b=41\), then modulo \(3\) gives \(a\) odd. For \(a\ge 3\), modulo \(8\) gives \(-3^b\equiv 1\pmod 8\), so \(3^b\equiv 7\pmod 8\), impossible. The case \(a=1\) fails directly.

If \(3^b-2^a=41\), then modulo \(3\) gives \(a\) even, and modulo \(4\) gives \(b\) even. Write \(a=2m,b=2n\). Then
\[
(3^n-2^m)(3^n+2^m)=41.
\]
Since \(41\) is prime, this forces \(3^n-2^m=1\) and \(3^n+2^m=41\), giving \(3^n=21\), impossible.

Thus \(41\) cannot be written in the required form.

\[
\boxed{41}
\]
